query: Consider the following context: High entropy alloys have excellent wear resistance, so they have great application prospects in the fields of wear resistance and surface protection. In that context, which material can be used for adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, and why?

generation.hypothesis: A high entropy alloy with a modified surface, specifically a CrMnFeCoNi alloy with a nanocrystalline coating, can be used to adhere to the surface of a Cu matrix, enhancing its wear resistance and surface protection properties.
generation.intervention: Deposition of a 5 μm thick nanocrystalline CrMnFeCoNi alloy coating on the Cu surface using magnetron sputtering at 300°C
generation.conditions: Vacuum atmosphere, 10^-3 Pa pressure, and 100 W power
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a strong metallurgical bond between the CrMnFeCoNi alloy coating and the Cu matrix
generation.mechanism: Diffusion of Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, and Ni atoms into the Cu matrix, creating a gradient of composition and enhancing adhesion
generation.predicted_outcome: An increase in adhesion strength of at least 20% compared to a bare Cu surface, with a corresponding decrease in wear rate of 15% under dry sliding conditions
generation.boundary: Adhesion strength > 20 MPa, wear rate < 10^-4 mm^3/Nm
generation.uncertainty: The actual adhesion strength and wear rate may vary depending on the specific deposition conditions, coating thickness, and testing parameters

falsification_experiment.design: Scratch test and dry sliding wear test
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured adhesion strength is less than 15 MPa or the wear rate is greater than 1.2 x 10^-4 mm^3/Nm, the hypothesis is falsified
